Titan Industrial Equipment Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Titan Industrial Equipment Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Titan Industrial Equipment's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ramirez, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Titan Industrial Equipment's performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, navigating a resilient demand environment across our core end markets while executing on our strategic priorities. Our diversified exposure to construction, mining, agriculture, and general manufacturing—which together account for about 85% of our $4.2 billion revenue base—has proven to be a key strength, with overall equipment order intake up 8% year-over-year to $1.1 billion, supported by a healthy $3.8 billion backlog that's grown 12% sequentially.

In construction, which made up 42% of Q3 revenue and rose from 38% a year ago, demand stayed robust on sustained infrastructure spending and non-residential activity. Globally, shipments grew 6% per Off-Highway Research, and we matched that with 7% higher bookings for excavators and wheeled loaders. North America's Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act kept delivering, with $52 billion in federal highway and bridge funding year-to-date lifting rental fleet utilization to 82% from 76%. Compact track loaders and telehandlers saw strong OEM orders, like from United Rentals, up 15% amid data center builds in the Southeast. EMEA grew 9% on the EU's €750 billion NextGenerationEU fund for rail and renewables, where our dozers and motor graders gained share. APAC softened to 3% due to China's real estate issues, but we're shifting to Southeast Asia, adding $150 million to our pipeline from Indonesian tenders. We're pushing electrification too, with our 50-ton battery-electric excavator prototype—co-developed with ABB—finishing Texas trials, promising 30% lower total cost of ownership, and eyeing H1 2025 rollout.

Mining, at 28% of revenue and flat year-over-year, dealt with commodity swings, but global demand held at 1-2% growth per AECOM. Copper at $4.20 per pound supported capex, though iron ore's drop to $105 per tonne hit Australia and Brazil. Our haul truck and drill rig orders rose 4% to $320 million, helped by 14% aftermarket growth on 85% fleet utilization. U.S. copper miners like Freeport-McMoRan drove North American strength, where our 400-ton autonomous trucks with Modular Mining's DISPATCH took 22% share, adding $80 million backlog. LatAm was steady at 2%, APAC down 3% on coal slowdowns. Our $200 million in next-gen HPGR crushers is gaining ground—pilots at BHP's Escondida show 15% more ore at lower energy, setting up $500 million in orders through 2026.

Agriculture, 18% of revenue and down slightly from 20%, cooled on farm income normalization and destocking, with tractor shipments off 5% per AEM. U.S. row crop pressures from $4.10 per bushel corn cut large tractor orders 10%, but our precision ag tools like RTK sprayers and autonomous tractors grew 6%. EMEA rose 4% on EU subsidies and dairy strength, with 12% forage harvester gains in Germany and France. Brazil's sugarcane uptick helped LatAm to 7%, while APAC was flat. Our Level 4 ag robots, tested on Midwest farms, cut labor 25% and chemicals 18%, and TitanLink telematics on 40% of fleets unlocks $300 million recurring software by FY26.

Manufacturing rounded it out at 12% of revenue, up 15%, on reshoring and automation. Global material handling demand surged 12% per VDMA, with U.S. factory capex at $1.2 trillion annualized per ISM. Our forklifts and AGVs booked $120 million, up 18%, including Tesla Nevada wins. China's PMI at 50.2 aided APAC at 10%, EMEA 8%. The $450 million European palletizer acquisition adds high-speed robotics with 99.9% uptime via AI maintenance.

Overall, our 62% aftermarket mix—up from 58%—gives visibility, with $2.6 billion in parts and service up 11% on digital twins and diagnostics. North America anchors 55% of backlog, but a new $150 million Changzhou plant targets 25% APAC growth in electric drivetrains. With 15% R&D spend versus the industry's 8%, on hydrogen and 5G fleets, we expect mid-single-digit demand growth into 2025 at 75% backlog conversion.

Looking ahead, we're at the intersection of Industry 4.0, electrification, and reshoring. Near-term, global end-market demand for industrial equipment grows 3-5% through early 2025, then accelerates to 7-9% CAGR through 2028, backed by our $2.8 billion backlog at 1.15x book-to-bill. Near-term caution prevails with ISM PMI around 48-50 and capex discipline post the boom-bust.

Semis and electronics, 25% of mix, surge 15-20% on CHIPS and AI data centers—TSMC and Intel ramps boost our CNC and wafer handlers to 12-15% growth. Automotive, 20%, flat to 2% as EV tempers ICE down 5-7%, offset by gigafactories. Aerospace/defense, 15%, 4-6% on aircraft ramps and F-35. Construction/mining, 15%, 1-3% with IIJA floor. Oil/gas flat, renewables 5%.

Medium-term, markets expand to $750 billion at 7-9% CAGR on digital transformation, sustainability, nearshoring. Digitization at 10-12% with our IoT PLCs and edge AI. Electrification 12-15% for gearboxes, actuators, hydrogen. Reshoring lifts U.S. PMI ex-China 20%.

North America 4% near-term, 8-10% medium on IRA/CHIPS. Europe 2% near, 7% medium on green deals. APAC China 3-5%, India 10%+. LatAm 6-8%.

Our pillars: $150 million capex for AI cobots, 5G handling; sustainability with low-carbon forging; M&A like $300 million German robotics for 85% utilization.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Turning to our financial performance, Titan Industrial Equipment reported $4.2 billion in revenue for the third quarter, representing an 11% increase year-over-year on a reported basis and 12% at constant currency, excluding a $25 million FX headwind. Gross margin expanded to 38.2%, driven by pricing discipline up 5.5%, aftermarket mix at 62%, and productivity from digital supply chain tools, though tempered 220 basis points by supply premiums and freight. Operating expenses were $1.1 billion, resulting in operating income of $480 million and an operating margin of 11.4%. Net income was $350 million, or $1.85 per share.

Breaking out growth, organic revenue rose 7.5%, accelerating from 6.2% in Q2—our strongest since Q4 2022—broad-based across segments. Machinery & Automation, 55% of revenues with CNC lathes, robotic welders, and hydraulic presses, grew 8.2% organically, led by 12% aftermarket on IndusConnect IoT across 28,000 assets up 35%, with 1.15x book-to-bill and $4.2 billion backlog. Energy & Infrastructure at 6.8% on data center chillers up 22%. North America added 4.8 points, EMEA 1.7, APAC 1.0 from India semis. Mining earthmovers dipped 2%, offset by 3.2% pricing.

Inorganic added 4.5 points or $125 million, led by Q1's $450 million RoboForge Dynamics for $85 million contribution, ahead of plan with $12 million synergies. FY23 tuck-ins like AeroTech Valves and Pacific WeldSys were accretive at 150bps EPS. We target 3-5% market cap in tuck-ins under $500 million for automation/sustainability, with $1.2 billion dry powder.

Supply chain-wise, we've seen improvements after pandemic resets, geopolitics, Red Sea issues adding 10-15 days to shipping. Our BOM—18% semis, 22% steel alloys, 12% electronics—had Q1 leads at 22-26 weeks, now 16-20 weeks, down 25% QoQ. OTD from top suppliers hit 85% from 72%, aiding 12% backlog growth to $1.45 billion, 65% convertible in 12 months.

Semis eased 30% with TSMC/Infineon ramps; PLC leads to 18 weeks, inventory at 120 days. Steel at $650/ton HRC, aluminum dual-sourced. Freight down 18% to $3,200/FEU. North America reshoring covers 40% steel at 10-12 weeks; APAC Vietnam fills gaps; Europe fixed with ThyssenKrupp.

We spent $85 million YTD on resilience—AI forecasting via SAP/ChainGuard at 92% accuracy, dual-sourcing 80% Tier 1, 51% aluminum stake for 150bps margins, safety stock 110 days, Mexico fab cutting Asia 12%. Premiums cost $22 million, freight $15 million, offset by 7% pricing.

Forward, leads to 14-16 weeks by year-end, ISM easing to 52 supports 18-22% 2025 growth.

Automation and digital revenues surged 32% to $1.45 billion, 38% of mix up from 29%, with hardware up 25% to $950 million and SaaS ARR 48% to $520 million at 78% margins, segment at 52% up 420bps. Digital Twins with PTC/Siemens cut customer downtime 27%, defects 18%, OEE to 91%, energy 15-20%. North America 35% on CHIPS, EMEA 42% on Digital Decade, APAC 22% India/Vietnam. $250 million capex for gen AI HMIs cutting setups 35%, edge acquisition for FactoryTalk middleware. 25-30% FY24 growth, ARR $750 million.

For guidance: Q4 revenue $2.25-$2.30 billion, 15% YoY up. Full year $8.65-$8.75 billion, 9-10% growth up $150 million midpoint on orders. Q3 was $2.15-$2.20 billion, 12-14% YoY flat-up 2% sequential. Automation 35% mix mid-teens on cobots/CNC to EV fabs, $450 million orders including $120 million Ford BlueOval. North America 45% mix on aerospace, EMEA 30% 5%, APAC 25% 10% India steel. ApexEdge IoT at 60% shipments, 28% service attach up 400bps, ElectroFlow 25% energy cut.

Operating margins: Q4 12.0-13.0%, up 150-250bps from Q3 10.8% on ERP/digital full benefit—4% throughput, 2.5pts cost cut. Pricing mid-single, aftermarket 28% at 22%. FY24 11.5-12.5%, 200bps expansion from 9.7%, on digital twins 18% less downtime, 88% utilization, e-drives 50bps. Aftermarket digital 25% growth to 30% revenue FY26.

We are committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and generating consistent cash flow.

Now, I will hand over to David Ramirez, COO, for an operational update.

David Ramirez (COO):
Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've been focused on optimizing our supply chain, improving manufacturing efficiency, and enhancing customer service. Supply chain resilience has been key, with AI-driven forecasting and nearshoring driving OTD to 85% and inventory turns improving. We've leveraged data analytics across our plants, from Ohio expansions to Mexico fabs, identifying 15-20% efficiency gains in routings and throughput. Employee training in Industry 4.0 skills has built a workforce ready for smart factories, with zero-based budgeting supporting wage investments while controlling costs.

And I will turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, David. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. Our TitanEdge platform and predictive maintenance tools are central, with digital twins optimizing lines for 27% less downtime and 15-20% energy savings. We're advancing autonomy in haul trucks and ag robots, electrification in excavators and drivetrains, and edge AI for cobots. Our new ElectroFlow hydraulic systems and SmartForge suite are exceeding expectations, with 91% OEE gains and 40% attach rates, driving 32% segment growth and positioning us for the smart factory era.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you discuss the trends you are seeing in automation spending?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Good morning, Alex. Automation spending remains a bright spot, aligning with labor shortages and reshoring. We're seeing 40%+ attach rates in automotive, aerospace, and semis, with 35% North America growth on CHIPS fabs, 42% EMEA on Mittelstand digitization, and strength in Vietnam electronics. Our cobots, PLCs, and TitanEdge IoT are delivering 27% downtime cuts and 18% defect reductions, fueling 32% segment growth. We expect 25-30% continuation into FY24 as brownfield upgrades accelerate.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee (Goldman Sachs):
What is your strategy for managing inflation and rising input costs?

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Jordan. Inflation management ties to our supply chain resilience—dual/tri-sourcing 80% BOM, reshoring 40% steel, fixed contracts like ThyssenKrupp. We've passed through 5.5-7% pricing, offsetting 8% steel/aluminum hikes and $37 million premiums/freight. Productivity from ERP/digital shaved 2.5pts costs, aftermarket at 62% mix buffers. Hedging 80% FX, zero-based budgeting control wages. Backlog pricing up 9% hedges, supporting margin guide.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Taylor Kim (Morgan Stanley):
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce your carbon footprint?

Mark Thompson:
Absolutely, Taylor. Sustainability is core, with 15% R&D on hydrogen fuel cells, 5G fleets, low-carbon forging, regen hydraulics. Digital tools cut customer energy 15-20%, ElectroFlow 25% less use. 40% portfolio ISO 14001+, aligning with EU CBAM/ETS, IRA. Electrification pilots like battery excavators target 30% TCO drop, HPGR crushers lower energy. Changzhou plant for electric drivetrains, aftermarket diagnostics boost ESG efficiency. We're leaders in the energy transition.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Closing Remarks:

Mark Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Titan Industrial Equipment. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
